title: The Number of Good Subsets
summary: Given an integer array, count the number of distinct subsets whose product is a product of one or more distinct prime numbers, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given an integer array, count the number of distinct subsets whose product is a product of one or more distinct prime numbers, modulo 10^9 + 7. A subset is any array formed by deleting some elements from the original array. Subsets are considered different based on the indices of elements deleted.
constraints: nums has 1 through 100000 values from 1 through 30.
A good subset’s product contains one or more distinct primes, with no squared prime factor.
Index choices distinguish subsets; return the count modulo 1000000007.
hints: Represent the prime factors of every square-free value 2..30 as a ten-bit mask.
Use subset DP over used-prime masks; skip values containing a squared prime and multiply transitions by their occurrence count.
Seed dp[0]=2^count(1); for each value, add dp[state]*count[value] to disjoint state|mask.
A good subset maps uniquely to disjoint selected prime masks and index choices; descending mask transitions use each numeric value group once.
editorial: A good subset maps uniquely to disjoint selected prime masks and index choices; descending mask transitions use each numeric value group once.

tests.explanation: The six valid index subsets use two or three, optionally with the one; four is invalid because it repeats prime two.
The five good subsets combine the square-free values without repeating a prime factor.
